steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: Sure and steady, you hear me?

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: This is your last chance before I kick you outta here.

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Questionable Man
steps.text: That's right, slow and steady—

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: ...Ahh!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I told you to be sure and steady! Now you've gone and ruined another one.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Just copy the pattern on the wax paper. It's not that hard.

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: I didn't mean to ruin it, Consultant. It's just, the scribblings are all weird and complicated...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Those are words. It says, 'Get 20% off with this coupon.'

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: I know those are words, and I know you're printing coupons, but like I told you, I can't read...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Alright, fine, never mind.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: But forget about your wages. You're lucky I'm not asking you to pay for all the ruined wax paper.

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, why don't you do it yourself?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Because I've got a bunch of other things to do, and I don't have the time to fiddle with wax paper—

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Consultant! There's another gang fight out there!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: See?

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: ...Fine.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, you wasted all my wax paper, but I guess you put in the work. You can grab a couple of potatoes from that sack over there. Can't have people calling me a miser.

steps.name: Dejected Man
steps.text: Really? Thanks, Consultant!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Who's fighting who this time, Liz?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Over a few damn rocks again? I've practically memorized a script for breaking up fights now.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Say, Liz, want to try your hand at etching wax paper?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: I thought you ran out.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, I just remembered I actually had an extra pack lying around.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: A likely story. Anyway, I'm not doing it. Words make my head hurt.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: But I'm curious. Why did you get a printer when you knew you couldn't afford to found a newspaper?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Okay, don't tell anyone. You know the food trader asked us to print some coupons, right? Four pieces of scrap metal for one bag of potatoes.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: You want to print extra coupons?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Only a moron would ruin his own reputation like that.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He's printing this because scrap metal is in short supply, and he has a basement full of potatoes. What we're printing, though, is not 'scrap metal for potatoes', but '20% off'.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: I see... you want to trade with other stuff? Maybe wood? We've got plenty of that lying around.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Depends on the current prices.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: You always see further than anyone else.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I see so far ahead that I forgot nobody here can write.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Speaking of which, I hear a reading class just opened.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Reading class? Oh, you mean that merc. Doesn't look like somebody you'd wanna mess with. Might think about it, if one of his students strikes out on their own.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Fat chance. It's all kids even younger than me. He probably has his hands full just keeping them in their seats.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Kids? Doesn't sound like he's trying to make a living out of it...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: So why did he start the class at all?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Out of some big dreams, maybe? I've got a relative whose kid goes there. He says the teacher talks about Kazdelian culture, our future, stuff like that.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Great, now I'm sure we won't get along.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Well, you can start etching your wax paper right away. Plenty of work for one person.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hey, I was joking. I'm not about to let someone like that slip through my fingers.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Ooh, getting serious, aren't we?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: So, what's the plan, Consultant?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Quiet, I'm thinking.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Is Mr. Hoederer in?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hi there, Mr. Hoederer. My name's Pohl, and I live around here.
Pohl looks around the room. The only notable feature is a blackboard with a few basic sentences written on it, plus some children's scribblings on the side.
There are also a few old, tattered books.
Seeing this, Pohl is even more certain that he has the right plan for talking to the guy.
He rubs his hands and deliberately avoids looking into Hoederer's eyes.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I apologize for the abrupt visit, but I...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I have a dream.
Pohl chooses to look to Hoederer's face after this statement. However, he reads no notable emotion upon it.
Not much of a surprise. People willing to do things like this tend to be a little eccentric. Perhaps he is just not the talkative type.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I've heard that you have the same dream. You're teaching the next generation of Kazdel to read, right?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: That's my dream too. A Kazdel where everyone can read.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Honestly, you're one step ahead of me. You're doing great work here.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Teaching some wild kids in a tiny room like this... you are a dreamer, sir, and I respect you for that.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Sarkaz culture has been lost to us for too long. Kazdel has to learn the importance of writing, culture, and civilization again. And it all starts with education.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: All you have, though, is one little classroom. Pretty easy to fail here.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Word of mouth can get distorted, disappear. That's why I cobbled together a printer.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (His eyes lit up! This is gonna work.)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Think about it. It takes seconds to print what takes you an hour to say, and you can reach more people this way. That's what you should be aiming for.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: So I came to you. To ask you to spare some time to help with etching wax paper for my type, to give your dream a leg up.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'd do it myself, but there are other things that need my attention—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You can read?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Yes, the work needs reading...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Wait, that's not what I meant, I mean—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: In order to read... no, we were talking about wax paper...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Wax paper... wax paper—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Wait, what was you question?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You asked me if I could read?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Er, yes, I can.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Who taught you to read? Your parents? A teacher? Are they still in Kazdel?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: ...I taught myself.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You're self-taught? That's impressive. I haven't met a literate Sarkaz in these parts for a long time.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: ...Same here.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I mean, I'm just as happy to meet you, Mr. Hoederer.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Back on topic, I wanted to ask you to help contribute to a Kazdel where everyone can read. Your classroom is an achievement, of course, but—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You said you built a printer? What are you printing?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Just stuff I think is useful, brochures, local news—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Can anybody else read them?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: That's certainly an issue. And it's why I print other things, discount coupons for example. Don't need to be able to read, as long as the food trader has a sample to refer to.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's not exactly in line with my vision, but that's all I can do on my own, which is why I came to you—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: On the contrary, there's a great deal of power in words that can be traded for food.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: ...Power?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, talking to you sure is enlightening, Mr. Hoederer. Now, about the wax paper...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I'll go when I have time.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, a little etching here and there wouldn't quite be enough. I truly want to make this a real print shop. Could we set a more regular time? Like a few afternoons each week?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I have other business besides the literacy class. I can't offer you too much time.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, if you'll pardon my frankness... we must all make sacrifices for our dreams.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: And, a dream is not something measured so simply in terms of time, is it?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: All the gangs around here know I can read, so they come to me whenever they need something read or calculated, like figuring out who gains money and who loses...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Yet I've squeezed out the time to open this print shop. Sure, it cuts into my leisure, but...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (No... that won't work. Seems like he's for-real busy.)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Perhaps you could let me know what's eating up your time? I might be able to help you deal with it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: (Wry smile) Thanks, but no thanks.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (No, I can't back off now. At least...)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Sorry, Mr. Hoederer.)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: We're really shorthanded. If you couldn't help... I'm afraid this print shop venture has to come to an end...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'm really at my wits' end, and I don't want the printer to go to waste. If even you can't help me...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: So you need a typesetter right now, no matter what?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Yes. If you really can't spare the time, maybe we can find another solution together? I've spent all my savings on the printer.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You know what the gangs are like. I end up owing them money, after all I've done for them. Never mind the printer; I'll be out of a place to live if I can't keep this running.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Mr. Hoederer?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: How about this.
Hoederer turns around and goes to a corner of the room. His tall frame obscures what he is doing.
Pohl feels his heart race.
What is he getting? A letter? An address? Perhaps... a weapon?
Couldn't possibly be money—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Here, this money should last a while. Just pay me back when you're able, take your time.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I know that paying with money in Kazdel isn't easy, but it should be enough to pay the gangs off.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Use the rest of it to hire someone, teach them to read and write, so there'll be another literate person in these parts.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No, I mean, yes, I could do that, but this money is...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I saved it together with someone. I didn't touch her part. This is all coming from my share.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: But... aren't you worried that I'll just take the money and—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Bite your tongue, Pohl! There's cash right in front of you!)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Guess I'll... take it?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Take it.
Pohl stands dumbfounded with the money in his hand. Hoederer steps to his side and bends down to pat his shoulder.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: How old are you, kid?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's alright if you don't want to say.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You taught yourself to read and write. I was just thinking about that.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No parent, no teacher. What kind of life drove a Kazdelian kid to learn to read and write on his own?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Go home now. And I want a copy of whatever you print, once you find your typesetter.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Mr. Hoederer, I—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No, forget it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: You're back, Consultant! How did it go with the merc?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: What's with the face? If he said no, he said no.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: He... didn't say no.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Even better!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's not like that. He—

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: What is it? You're not acting like yourself. Did he hit you or something?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Did he have a bunch of books that even you couldn't read?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: No, that's not—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: —Oh yeah, books.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Give me a hand, Liz.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: I said I'm not helping with the wax paper.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'll take care of the paper. There's a sliding door under my bed. Inside is a wooden box.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Wow, I didn't know you had a hiding spot like this! What's in it? Jewels? Pure Gold? A Sankta gun?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You'll know when you see it. Just grab it for me while I check the printer.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Wow, this is heavy. What the heck is in it?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here's the key, open it up. I've got ink all over my hands.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Well, guess I should be glad that you trust me.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: What's with all the old books?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Oh, I thought this was Mr. Hoederer's home...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's for you.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Pohl? Come in.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here, Mr. Hoederer.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Printouts?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I printed a few books I used when I learned to read. They might be useful for your literacy class.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: From a decade ago?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Thanks. This will work nicely once the children have progressed a little further. Let me see... mercenary diaries, propaganda pamphlets from the Military Commission during the Leithanian invasion...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You've got all sorts of stuff here. This looks like a manuscript from around 1030.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Is it valuable? I'll bring the original, if you need it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No, the copy will do just fine. How much?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I couldn't possibly ask you for more money! I can't even spend everything you gave me, even after paying back the gangs.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here's half back.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Pohl—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Don't worry about the other half. I'll pay it back in a few months, with 10% interest.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ha. I'm sure we can cut the interest out?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Don't look at me. It's your money.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: In that case... could you make a printout of this map, Pohl?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Of course. Anything else?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Test papers for the kids, maybe?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: The wax paper's done, Consultant.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Mm... not bad. You're almost ready to get to work.

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: But I didn't understand half of what's on it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Don't worry, I wasn't much better when I started learning. Want some potatoes?

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: ...With sugar? Wow!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You're my only typesetter. Got to make sure you're happy and well-fed—

steps.name: Angry Gang Leader
steps.text: We had an agreement with them to split forty-sixty, but now they want fifty-fifty! You tell them they're greedy slugs, Consultant!

steps.name: Brooding Gang Leader
steps.text: Greedy slugs? Our guys bled for this!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Not again...

steps.name: Clever Girl
steps.text: It's always the same with these people, isn't it?

steps.name: Gang Leaders
steps.text: What did you say?!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Don't mind her, she's just a kid.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Anyway, this is simple.
Pohl takes out a printed sheet and slams it down on the table.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Here's your agreement. I have the hand-written original with palm-prints, and both of you have a copy.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Let me see... 'the profits shall be split 40-60...'

steps.name: Angry Gang Leader
steps.text: See? Written in black and white!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: 'In the event of any casualties, the side with fewer casualties shall relinquish part of their share, up to a 50-50 split...'

steps.name: Brooding Gang Leader
steps.text: Now THAT is black and white!

steps.name: Angry Gang Leader
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, you're not playing me for a fool, are you?

steps.name: Angry Gang Leader
steps.text: You're the only one who can read here! How do I know you didn't print this just to fool us? How do we know you're not full of shit?
Pohl grins and points at the door.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Why not learn to read and check for yourself?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: There's a merc who teaches reading classes over there. I hear he's still taking new students.
